title: Doorbell camera shows moment wind brought down trees, powerlines during Salt Lake storm

Doorbell camera footage from the Wasatch Hollow neighborhood in Salt Lake showed the moments wind brought down trees and powerlines on 1700 South. Doorbell camera footage from the Wasatch Hollow neighborhood in Salt Lake showed the moments wind brought down trees and powerlines on 1700 South.
"Sounded pretty much like a car crash," said Benjamin Bell, an area resident. "Like, you know, a large ka-blam! ""It was like super loud," Wells Archibald, another area resident, added. "Like, I heard it when I was coming home from school.
" People in the area described experiencing a heavy burst of wind, losing power, and coming out to see poles snapped in half and trees down all along the street. No cars seemed to be damaged.
"The wind, oh my goodness ... so loud and I was just like, 'What is going on? '" said Reilly Costello, who was visiting a friend in the area when the poles came down. "I'm from the Midwest, so I was like, 'This is tornado weather. '" Rocky Mountain Power told 2News roughly 100 customers were impacted by this specific incident, but more than 6,000 people across the state lost power Wednesday afternoon.
The poles on 1700 South were first reported down shortly after 3:00 p.m. "You look down the street, and there's more like just aged poles that could fall. They could fall that easily, as these other ones could fall too," said Megan Archibald, an area resident.
"So definitely need to do those, make new, get new ones. " "How often do these poles get checked? " 2News asked Rocky Mountain Power Spokesperson Jona Whitesides. "Everything, all of our stuff gets checked," Whitesides said.
"If it's kind of inside city proper, that can be anywhere from a year to 18 months. " 2News asked when these specific poles were last checked, and Whitesides said they would look into getting that information. "I don't know how it's going to get cleaned up very quickly and how these people are going to get power anytime soon," Megan Archibald said.
Rocky Mountain Power said it may take until the early morning hours of Thursday to get the area cleaned up and power restored.
